🇺🇸 Rubio is playing with fire, and his war on Nvidia could destroy America's AI boom

A stock market sell-off, Jensen Huang pushed out, and Washington preparing another round of restrictions on AI chip sales to China.

Economist Philip Pilkington believes these developments are connected.

His theory? This isn't simply about removing Jensen; it's about dismantling the company at the centre of America's AI revolution.

Philip accuses Rubio of pursuing a political crusade against China, arguing that the leak targeting Jensen was part of an effort to force a tougher approach to chip exports.

But there's a problem.

Nvidia isn't just another technology company; it's the financial engine helping keep the entire AI industry running.

Its chip revenues help fund investments across the sector, from ambitious start-ups to major technology companies.

Disrupt that flow of capital, Philip warns, and the damage spreads far beyond Nvidia.

And he suspects something even bigger is at stake.

A battle between open-source AI and powerful closed-source companies seeking to dominate the market.

Philip argues that open-source competition drives prices down, while closed-source providers have incentives to restrict competition, control data and lock customers into expensive systems.

He believes the campaign against Nvidia could benefit those seeking greater control over AI, but Washington may be destroying its own technological advantage in the process.

And China has another weapon: rare earth minerals and magnets.

If Beijing retaliates against renewed U.S chip restrictions, Philip fears the resulting supply-chain disruption could devastate American technology companies.

@philippilk

I’m deeply disappointed in the Rutgers Republicans Club’s decision to invite Greg Bovino to speak on campus. Giving him a platform is the wrong decision.
 
People can agree that border security is important and the need for immigration reform is urgent. They can also reject the cruel policies of officials like Greg Bovino that cost people their lives.

If the club moves forward with hosting Bovino, I will ensure the state works with Rutgers to protect the safety of everyone and the rights enshrined in our Constitution. I would hope that those in attendance use that opportunity to ask him why he chose cruelty over humanity and put Americans’ lives at risk in their own communities. They should also ask him what he makes of Americans’ overwhelming rejection of his policies in the midterms.

In New Jersey, we believe deeply in the values of this country. Those values do not include dehumanizing and cruel policies, and militias that pledge loyalty to the president instead of the Constitution. Maybe the only question to ask of Bovino is what part of his oath to the Constitution did he miss and how did he get so caught up in the group think of this Administration that he could justify ignoring his obligation to the very people he was meant to serve?
